stories.title: Ukraine becomes key 'exporter of instability' in Middle East — Russian diplomat
stories.summary: Russian Ambassador to Israel Anatoly Viktorov highlighted that the Kiev regime brazenly violated all the norms of international law
article_sentences: The Ukrainian regime is fueling instability in the Middle East, Russian Ambassador to Israel Anatoly Viktorov said.
"Today, Ukraine has become one of the world’s largest exporters of instability.
Kiev’s special services have their hands in many hotbeds of tension around the world, including in the Middle East.
Ukrainian ‘touring agents’ are actively trying to share their expertise," he said in a commentary released by the embassy’s press service.
"The Kiev regime brazenly violates all the norms of international law, including the International Convention for the Suppression of the Financing of Terrorism," he added.

stories.title: Part of Russia-US dialogue on Ukraine proceeds behind closed doors — RIAC director
stories.summary: Ivan Timofeyev cautioned against overemphasizing the roles of specific individuals
article_sentences: A substantial portion of the negotiations between Russia and the United States regarding Ukraine continues to unfold behind closed doors, Ivan Timofeyev, Director General of the Russian International Affairs Council (RIAC), has told TASS.

When asked whether US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner possess an understanding of how to resolve the conflict, Timofeyev responded: "Much of the negotiation process remains confidential, which is understandable; it’s a normal part of diplomatic efforts.
However, we have yet to observe any tangible results.
This indicates at best a stagnation in the process."
He cautioned against overemphasizing the roles of specific individuals - such as Witkoff and Kushner - whose planned visit to Russia, according to a TASS source, has been postponed.
"It’s positive that there’s some activity on the American side and attempts - albeit through trial and error - to identify a workable approach.
This contrasts with the approach of the Biden administration, which has not engaged in such efforts.
But making attempts is one thing; achieving results is another.
We have yet to see any," Timofeyev emphasized.
He further explained that the core challenge in resolving the conflict lies not in the personalities of the negotiators but in structural obstacles.
"The conflict itself is highly complex, and devising an algorithmic solution will be extraordinarily difficult.
